title: Graduated approval lanes and evidence bundling for go-live
content:
Purpose
This doc defines a graduated approval lanes model for release security sign-offs and a repeatable evidence-bundling automation for launches that involve RBAC v2 changes, audit-log schema updates, and SIEM export modifications. The goal is to make approval decisions faster, reduce ad-hoc evidence requests, and ensure consistent artifacts are produced for post-launch audits.

Scope
Applies to: hosted API and Dedicated releases, control-plane changes, SIEM pipeline changes, RBAC v2 role/permission schema migrations, and any change that touches production audit log format or export topology. Not intended for routine app code updates unless they include security configuration changes listed above.

High-level model: Graduated approval lanes
- Lane 0 (auto): Non-security-impacting builds. No security reviewer required. Evidence auto-archived for 7 days.
- Lane 1 (ops quick): Configuration-only changes (non-RBAC), minor SIEM filter updates, or audit-log label tweaks. Requires Ops lead + one security tech review item (30m SLA for acknowledgement). Evidence bundle required.
- Lane 2 (security review): RBAC v2 policy changes, audit-log schema non-backward-compatible changes, SIEM endpoint reconfiguration, or changes affecting KMS/HSM usage. Requires Security reviewer + SRE lead signoff.
- Lane 3 (executive/enterprise): Major data-handling changes, cross-region private-deployments, or enterprise-customer-impacting exceptions. Needs Security Director + Legal + Product signoff and recorded exception approval.

How lane is determined
- A lightweight risk classifier (script: tools/release/lane_classifier.py) runs on PR metadata and a short checklist answers. If uncertain, the release engineer picks the higher lane. The classifier is advisory only.

Pre-launch checklist (for Lane 1–3)
- RBAC v2: list changed roles, permission diffs, migration plan, and roll-back steps.
- Audit logs: exact schema diffs (field-level), retention policy changes, and example events pre/post change.
- SIEM export: exporter configuration (endpoint, TLS cert thumbprint, expected event rate), parsing rules (Logstash/Fluent config or ingest pipeline), and alert adjustments.
- Evidence bundle: automated snapshot of configs, sample events, infrastructure state, and signed approval template.
- Canary plan: traffic gating, fallbacks to previous variant, and smoke-test commands.
- Secrets & keys: confirm KMS/HSM rotations not required, or list required rotation steps.
- Compliance matrix: list affected controls (SOC2/ISO27001/PCI as applicable) and mapped mitigations.

RBAC v2 specific items (detailed)
- Role diffs: include CSV containing role_name, previous_permissions (comma list), new_permissions (comma list), and author.
- Migration strategy: whether migration is incremental (shadow + promote) or cutover. If cutover, provide pre-cutover dry-run outputs (apply --dry-run logs).
- Temporary elevation: any temporary exception requests must include expiration timestamp, approver name, and justification; temporary APIs must be proxied and logged.
- Least-privilege proof: small sampling of impacted token sessions showing no unexpected access (example logs tied into evidence bundle).
- Backout command set: explicit commands/PRs to revert role tables or re-run old role sync.

Audit log schema (summary mapping and expectations)
- Schema versioning: every change increments audit_schema_version (integer). New events must be backwards compatible or explicitly approved for version bump.
- Required event fields (must be present on all audit events): ["timestamp", "request_id", "actor_id", "actor_type", "actor_role_snapshot", "action", "resource_type", "resource_id", "auth_method", "outcome", "kv_cache_key_present", "sequence_len", "model_variant", "trace_id"]
- Recommended fields: ["region", "shard_id", "gpu_type", "model_checksum"]
- Field formats: timestamp = ISO8601 w/ timezone; request_id = uuid-v4; actor_id = internal_user:human|service:svc-name format; outcome = success|failure|partial.
- Example audit event (bundled as sample_event.json in evidence): one pre-change sample and one post-change sample for each modified pipeline step.
- Schema diff artifact: human-readable mapping and a machine-readable avro/jsonschema file (place under evidence/schema-diffs/).

SIEM export and ingestion notes
- Transport: TLS 1.2+ with mTLS preferred for Dedicated cust. Certificate thumbprint must be recorded in evidence bundle.
- Format: JSON lines (ndjson) with one audit event per line. Timezone normalization must be applied before export.
- Batching: exporter should use size-based batching with max 1MB per batch and max 500ms flush.
- Backpressure handling: failing SIEM endpoint must not drop audit events — write to local durable queue with retention policy of 72 hours, and alert paging on queue size trend.
- Parsing: supply SIEM (or ELK) ingest pipeline config snippet that maps our fields into canonical SIEM fields; include example grok/ingest config in evidence bundle.
- Tests: include an extract that simulates 10k events/min for 1 minute and verify SIEM ingest success rate >=99%. Attach load test results.

Evidence automation (how to produce the bundle)
- Evidence bundle artifact layout (zip):
  - metadata.json (human + machine fields: release_id, lane, approver, schema_version)
  - rbacs/role-diffs.csv
  - audit/schema-diffs/{{old}}-to-{{new}}-schema.json
  - examples/pre-change-*.ndjson
  - examples/post-change-*.ndjson
  - siem/ingest-pipeline.conf
  - canary/smoke-results.txt
  - signatures/ (PGP signatures or internal signing token output)
  - approvals/signoff-template.txt (filled)
- Automation tool: scripts/release/generate_evidence.sh runs the following:
  1) git checkout $PR_SHA
  2) ./infra/tools/collect-rbac-diff --out rbacs/role-diffs.csv
  3) ./infra/tools/export-audit-samples --before $PRE_SHA --after $PR_SHA --out audit/
  4) ./infra/tools/generate-schema-diff --old $PRE_SCHEMA --new $NEW_SCHEMA --out audit/schema-diffs/
  5) ./infra/tools/siem-config-export --env production --out siem/
  6) zip -r evidence-bundle-$RELEASE_ID.zip .
- CI integration: pipeline job name: security:evidence-bundle. It fails the PR if the bundle generator errors. Evidence bundle must be uploaded to the release artifact store and linked in the PR.

Exception approval flow (temporary or permanent exceptions)
- Small exceptions (Tier A): minor permission grant for <72 hours. Approver: SRE lead + Security on-call. Recorded in quick-exception log and auto-expire.
- Medium exceptions (Tier B): permissions or schema change that creates detectable risk but has mitigating controls (e.g., masked PII). Approver: Security engineer + Product manager. Requires evidence bundle and explicit rollback plan.
- Major exceptions (Tier C): enterprise-impacting or cross-control deviation. Approver: Security Director + Legal + Customer Success (if customer affected). Requires formal exception form (template in approvals/exception-form.md), and an audit ticket created (jira:SEC-EXC-xxxx).
- All exceptions must be tracked in the Exception Register (Confluence table) with required fields: exception_id, requestor, approver(s), lane, expiry, mitigation, linked_artifact.

Sign-off template (copy into approvals/signoff-template.txt)
- Release: {{RELEASE_ID}}
- PR: {{PR_URL}}
- Lane: {{LANE}}
- Evidence bundle: {{ARTIFACT_URL}}
- Approvals: (name / role / signature / timestamp)
- Noted exceptions: (Y/N; if Y -> link exception id)
- Final decision: GO / HOLD / ROLLBACK_REQUIRED
- Reviewer notes: freeform

Escalation & timeline expectations
- All Lane 2 reviews: initial reviewer response within 8 business hours. Final decision within 48 business hours.
- If review stalls, escalation path: security-oncall -> security-manager -> security-director. Use Slack escalation channel #sec-escalate.

Operational runbook excerpts (quick commands)
- Verify RBAC migrate dry-run output: ./infra/tools/role-sync --dry-run --input rbacs/role-diffs.csv | tee canary/dry-run.log
- Generate sample audit event: python infra/tools/make_audit_event.py --actor svc-deployer --action role_update --out examples/post-change-1.ndjson
- Revert RBAC: kubectl apply -f rbacs/rollback/roles-previous.yaml --context=prod
- Repoint SIEM exporter to holdback: ./infra/tools/siem-toggle --env prod --mode holdback --reason "rollback in progress"

Audit readiness & post-launch
- Immediately after go-live: run verification script security:evidence-verify that validates presence of required files in the evidence bundle and that sample events appear in SIEM within 60s.
- 24h check-in: security-runbook-scan (automated) and brief post-launch notes posted to Confluence page (template: SEC-GO-LIVE-POSTLAUNCH).
- 30-day review: if the change was an exception, ensure a post-implementation review is scheduled and closure is recorded.

Notes, references, and links
- Related Confluence pages: CONFLUENCE:SEC-APPR-LANES, CONFLUENCE:RBAC-V2-GUIDE, CONFLUENCE:AUDIT-SCHEMA-HIST
- Helpful scripts & locations: repo infra/tools, release scripts under tools/release, evidence pipeline in CI under .github/workflows/security-evidence.yml
- Slack threads: #sec-release (main), #sec-oncall (escalation), thread link: slack://channel?team=T1234&id=thread-3F7D2
- Example Jira tickets to reference: INFRA-4217 (rbac migration), SEC-1229 (siem ingest change), SEC-EXC-0123 (previous exception example).

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want to require mTLS for hosted API SIEM exports by default? (ops + security decision needed)
- Add a metric for evidence quality (percent of bundles accepted without follow-up).
- Update the auto-classifier to include model-variant-sensitive heuristics (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/601).

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] lane assigned and documented
- [ ] evidence bundle generated and uploaded
- [ ] RBAC diffs attached (role-diffs.csv)
- [ ] schema diffs attached (audit/schema-diffs)
- [ ] SIEM ingest config included (siem/ingest-pipeline.conf)
- [ ] canary smoke-tests with results attached
- [ ] approvers listed and signoff template populated
- [ ] exception form filled if applicable

End of doc
